Equipment is shared across the entire roster. A wizard also has one signature technique and one passive, outside the eight spells and six equipped slots.

Choose the wizard before a Conclave begins and keep that wizard throughout the match. Preparation changes equipment, equipped spells, and free augment choices, while preserving the casting language a player practiced. Training and custom duels permit unrestricted roster experiments. All 36 wizards start from 300 health, 100 mana, and 100 stamina; explicit passive exceptions apply only under their stated conditions. Difficulty is a learning estimate from 1 to 5, not a power rating.

## Casting language

Every wizard has a distinct execution method. The roster includes held focus, crest release, rune tracing, voice, token syntax, parry response, instrument rhythm, circuit routing, sigil geometry, pressure metering, phase selection, polarity alternation, anchor distance, footwork, melee weaving, stances, memory, delayed scheduling, orbit catching, thread weaving, frequency tuning, hand chords, tile swaps, packet division, reticle painting, ratio balance, ground contact, prediction alignment, velocity alignment, ritual walking, kinetic engraving, vitality pledges, conditional clauses, spatial rotation, event response, and cursor shepherding. The catalogue describes a normal cast, an optional mastery condition, and distinct vulnerabilities for each.

Normal casts are reliable. A low accuracy rune, imperfect beat, wrong branch, or off-center control widget never produces random backlash or turns a requested spell into a different spell. Where a correction is required, it occurs in the unpaid preparation stage and has a visible time cost. Guided normal preparation is available for the complex modes. Guidance completes a normal action and gives no mastery reward. The selected spell remains the selected spell.

The control protocol distinguishes preparation from commitment. During preparation, the game shows the selected spell, preparation progress, and exact input state. Cancellation before commitment spends no spell mana. Commitment pays the listed spell cost and starts its listed cooldown and intrinsic windup; it follows the spell's normal interruption policy. Wizard preparation does not silently eliminate an intrinsic windup. For wizards who begin casting with a movement/parry event, the triggering action uses its own normal stamina cost and recovery. Signature techniques use their listed activation and windup rather than requiring a second mastery puzzle.

Primary Cast, Cast Modifier, Modifier A, Modifier B, technique activation, item activation, and common movement/guard/melee bindings are independently remappable. No wizard overrides movement, sensitivity, FOV, sprint, jump, dodge, or common melee. Class-specific controls are interpreted only during an explicitly opened preparation state. A two-dimensional rune or vertex pane holds the camera only while its modifier is deliberately held, displays a camera-lock icon, and cancels instantly; releasing/canceling returns camera control without applying accumulated cursor movement. Direction-key tracing is an equivalent alternative. Corner widgets, pressure bars, circuits, and motif panes leave world aim live. Reticle-painting and prediction wizards deliberately move the real camera; their guides never aim or detect an enemy for the player.

## Mastery normalization and stacking

Mastery earns one specified benefit per cast: no more than 20% resource efficiency, or 15% damage/projectile-speed improvement. Individual roster rewards are normally 10–15%, with explicit qualifying windows and clear tells. A spell receives one grammar reward, not one reward for every token, syllable, mouse sample, target hit, or animation. Input faster than the stated accepted interval provides no additional benefit. Marks, orbit catches, and charges cannot be banked beyond their stated windows. Cosmetic input does not generate damage or mana.

All mastery-linked efficiency rewards, including equipment and augments that modify the same rewarded cast, clamp together at 20%. All mastery-linked direct damage, projectile-speed, or windup benefits clamp in their relevant category at the shared 15% improvement limit; speed changes do not secretly multiply across preparation and intrinsic windup. Different statistical categories still obey the full combat caps. Secondary/reaction damage is not eligible for grammar direct-damage bonuses unless an exact spell rule expressly defines it as part of that spell's primary payload. An augment that changes delivery inherits the source spell's one mastery result; recasts, reflected shots, splits, and delayed portions never earn a second result.

More difficult input does not raise base health or remove counterplay. A long phrase provides a longer exposed preparation than a quick focus cast. Parry and melee grammars need a genuine combat event. Movement grammars demand real distance, support, or velocity and cannot be activated by shaking keys against a wall. The mastery condition and the commitment cue are both visible to the caster; opponents receive consistent hand motion, sound, and release cues without seeing private guide answers.

## Voice and accessible input

Oren's voice mode uses a fixed phrase of three selected syllables with a 0.75-second cadence. Recognition distinguishes syllable identity and timing; accent, native language, pitch, loudness, vocal strain, and microphone price confer no combat multiplier. The game includes microphone calibration and a confidence preview outside matches. The caster may switch to an equivalent three-input rhythm phrase at any time outside a committed cast, including when recognition fails. Both modes have the same exposure, cue, reward, and technique/passive effects. The opponent hears the same game-generated phrase in both modes, with no private live-microphone leakage.

The phrase lexicon uses eight short fictional syllables: ka, lo, mi, na, pe, ru, se, and ti. Oren's eight phrases, assigned in local spell-index order, are ka-lo-mi, na-pe-ru, se-ti-ka, lo-mi-na, pe-ru-se, ti-ka-lo, mi-na-pe, and ru-se-ti. Technique activation has a separate audible cue. The entire spellbook is never a speech-recognition free-text task. Optional captions display the phrase and beat timing, and visual/haptic beat indicators replace audio cues.

Accessibility presets provide hold/toggle alternatives, one-handed logical-input selection, direction-key gesture entry, scalable guide graphics, color-independent symbols, audio-independent frequency gauges, and static memory guides. Full-power alternative controls preserve the qualifying commitment and precision task; guided assistance provides reliable normal casts. Ranked rules do not reward raw physiology. Simultaneous chord recognition supports a single-selector confirmation mode with the same timing requirement and telegraph. Mouse gestures use normalized coordinates so DPI, resolution, and device polling rate never change the score. Inputs are locally timestamped and server-validated under the game's bounded latency compensation; a better microphone never grants a wider combat acceptance window.

## Equipment and environmental behavior

All wizards may equip every wand, staff, weapon, armor, magical clothing, boot, trinket, and consumable. A focus changes the visible grip and its stated equipment effects while preserving the wizard's casting language. A weapon-wielding voice mage still speaks or taps; a staff-wielding spellblade still performs its defined common melee profile. The Main Focus and Sidearm restrictions and active-item cap apply to all 36 equally. Equipment never grants another wizard's exclusive spell.

Physical fields remain neutral: water, steam, ice, wind, projectile-slowing screens, crossing strips, and displacement lines affect both fighters. Personal shield buffs and expressly self-following guardians have the stated personal owner; they do not change the allegiance of the world reaction beneath them. A caster can be caught by their own slow strip or helped by an opponent's wind lane. Ritual guides and preparation panes have no hidden collision, reaction strength, reveal, damage, or enemy-detection function. Actual signature walls, circles, rods, seals, and lanes use the shared three-field cap; signature summons use the two-summon cap and remain visible and destructible.

## Training, feedback, and roster balance targets

Every wizard has a casting classroom with normal-cast tutorial, isolated mastery drill, moving-target drill, approach/escape drill, and a reaction-room scenario using that kit's own spells. A first-time player can practice the eight base spells before building any augment combination. The grammar overlay reports exactly why mastery was missed: late beat, wrong order, incorrect ratio, broken tether, insufficient travel, or inaccurate stroke. It never reports merely “bad cast.” Training can slow the simulation and replay inputs; slowing is unavailable in live matches.

The spellbook shows normal and mastered output, preparation time, intrinsic windup, resource cost, range, and clear counterplay. A wizard's eight cards remain searchable by effect, delivery, school, and reaction tag. Two spell-specific augment branches per spell create 16 possible wizard transformations; these are free draft choices, not spell purchases. Branch compatibility and ongoing eligibility are shown before selection. Any dormant branch retains its slot and displays the missing item, parent, or explicitly required equipped-spell condition. A simple own-spell predicate means ownership, so a transformation of an unequipped but owned spell remains acquired and applies as soon as that spell is equipped in a later preparation.

## Spell transformation resolution

The 864 free augments comprise 288 universal definitions and 576 wizard spell transformations. Each wizard has exactly two authored transformation choices for each of its eight spells. A rank-2 choice consumes a free draft selection and retains rank 1 with the listed exceptions; it never repeats the entire source cast or consumes Crowns. Each wizard's transformation pool spans all three rarities. The latter half of the roster has five Silver, six Gold, and five Prismatic choices per wizard, ensuring the wizard-transformation guarantee is supported at every draft rarity.

Every transformation names its exact source spell, exact eligible wizard, rank-1 behavior, rank-2 behavior, tradeoff, and counterplay. Numeric source fields not changed in the transformation are inherited: mana, cooldown, intrinsic cast time, range, primary damage, channel, and reaction strength. A changed delivery never silently doubles the original payload. “Half damage” means half of the source's current primary payload after applicable modifiers, with the stated source total cap. New secondary damage has one generation of recursion and cannot trigger resource, on-kill, lifesteal, or other direct-hit rewards unless a global rule explicitly allows it. A source spell and all its delayed/split portions receive one casting-mastery result.

Alternate delivery branches share an explicit exclusive group and cannot be equipped together. Compatible branches have no exclusive group and apply in ascending augment-ID order: shape/delivery edits first, payload behavior second where authored. If both branches split the same source, splitting is a single operation and the stricter projectile count and shared payload cap win; it cannot multiply twice. Timing, condition, and recast changes remain explicit and visible in the combined spell card. A new field, trap, panel, or summon consumes the normal allocation unless the record expressly defines a connected shared allocation. On cap exhaustion, source creation follows the normal oldest-owned replacement policy and never grants an extra hidden field.

Recasts use the spell-recast binding and do not occupy equipment-active slots. They add no charge, mana, damage, or immunity beyond the authored rule. Manual detonation adds its listed final warning and respects hard-control immunity. A reflected, recalled, tangent, returning, or waypoint projectile is still blocked by solid geometry and never acquires an unseen target. Field movement, neutral trap triggering, branch conditions, and historical combat events are server-owned. Destroying an anchor cancels the dependent effect whenever its rule requires that anchor.

Loadout validation displays the combined range, commitment, cost, payload cap, reaction strength, field/summon use, and branch conflicts before the player accepts a draft choice. The training room can preview every rank of every spell transformation without granting it in a competitive match.

Balance evaluation uses equal-skill duel win rate, skill-bracket win rate, effective approach/escape success, resource efficiency, mastery completion rate, voice-versus-rhythm equivalence, disabled-accessibility-mode equivalence, and matchup spread across arena sizes. The numeric values in this design are tuning targets, not tested results. Matchup adjustments preserve each wizard's control language and readable weakness rather than homogenizing the roster.


# Exclusive spell rules and transformation profiles

There are 288 exclusive base spells, eight for each wizard. Each base record specifies owner, school, role, channel, mana cost, cooldown, intrinsic windup, range, damage, delivered effect, world interaction, counterplay, and tags. The base kit is available immediately and equips six spells. No shop purchase, equipment effect, shared augment, steal, copy, or summon grants another wizard’s spell.

## Numerical interpretation

Mana and cooldown are paid at commitment. The cast-time field measures intrinsic windup after the wizard’s preparation. Range is the maximum valid targeting or travel range, measured in meters; a self-centered action uses range zero and its description supplies radius or reach. Damage is a deliberately explicit expression when a spell has direct, splash, channel, or conditional components. Read its cap and whether hits are exclusive: a target cannot receive direct and splash twice when the record prohibits it.

A projectile’s speed, footprint, lifetime, release cue, and collision behavior come from its effect text. Beams and rays stop at declared solid geometry. A reflection uses one bounce and 70 percent retained damage unless a modifier with a declared tradeoff explicitly changes that result within its source budget. Summons need visible targets, destructible bodies, bounded range and lifetime; they cannot read a hidden enemy or acquire through steam.

World strength numbers refer to heat, water, frost, dust, wind, force, or other bounded source states. Repeated ticks consume the same cast budget instead of generating new material indefinitely. An effect that divides into several pieces divides its original strength unless the augment explicitly adds a separately paid strength unit. Neutral material reactions affect both players. Personal buffs and deliberately bound spell constructs retain their explicit target filters.

## Spell tags

Every spell has a namespaced school tag such as `school:light`, plus its bare school affinity for browsing. A damaging spell has `damaging` and its channel tag, such as `channel:arcane`. School and damage channel remain distinct. A direct spell may be thermal while another spell from the same school supplies arcane defense. School tags do not invent a second damage payload.

Delivery tags include projectile, ray, beam, cone, melee, field, trap, summon, dash, teleport, movement, and channel as appropriate. Rays also qualify as beams; dash and teleport imply movement. Shield or defense spells qualify as defensive. Offensive melee spells or offensive range at most six meters qualify as close; offensive range at least twelve meters qualifies as ranged. Those derived tags appear explicitly in the catalogue, so eligibility does not depend on an undocumented label.

Summon mobility has its own tags. Stationary means the summoned body remains where placed; mobile means it follows an orbit, route, movement record, or command. It does not describe whether the wizard may walk while casting. A rooted shrub and fixed wisps are stationary; a routed paper familiar or moving blade is mobile. A transformation changing that movement updates the structural profile before shared tag conditions are evaluated. Wind-producing effects carry wind only when they actually supply a declared wind source.

## Layered spell forms

Every base spell has two dedicated augment choices. Mutually exclusive branches have the same nonempty exclusivity group; compatible branches can operate together in catalogue order. Rank 2 retains rank 1 except for its explicitly replaced parameters. Inherited mana, cooldown, range, channel, geometry, and payload remain the base values unless a branch changes them. A second rank never duplicates the entire original spell or grants another activation key.

For eligibility, build a structural profile using the equipped base spells, enabled wizard transformations, and chosen equipment structural effects. General shared augments cannot create their own prerequisite tags. A projectile-to-trap branch removes projectile and adds field/trap; a stationary-to-moving summon branch exchanges stationary for mobile. For actual combat, apply all active general augments to that resolved structure, then mastery and global caps. Shared-to-shared requirements use owned-augment IDs, rank, tags, or family predicates.

One trajectory form is active at a time when branches conflict. Equipment splitting, return routing, ricochet, and portal routing cannot multiply each other without an explicit compatibility rule. Priority is the chosen wizard trajectory branch, then the chosen equipment trajectory mode, then ordinary parameter modifiers. Dormant incompatible effects are shown before combat. Compatible payload, reaction, or timing branches can combine under the original spell’s event identity and global proc budgets.

## Telegraph and counterplay

A transformed spell has an altered cue describing its actual delivery. Converting a ray into a ground trap shows placement and arming; adding a recast shows a pending state; changing a shield to a directional panel exposes its back; moving a rooted summon exposes its route. An opponent’s inspection describes the final form rather than only the base card.

The catalogue is the complete content definition, with global constraints supplying omitted common recovery and stricter ceilings. Numeric values are tuning targets. Verification must exercise each transformed form and its declared combinations against terrain, guard, concealment, hard-control immunity, world-state order, and resource accounting.


# Shared equipment rules

All 120 equipment definitions are shared across the 36 wizards. Equipment never requires a particular wizard and never unlocks another wizard’s base spell. A focus changes grip, common weapon profile, and its stated modifier while preserving the selected wizard’s casting method. Every item uses the same Crown price for every wizard. Conditional effects may have better synergy with some kits, but there is no private class equipment pool.

## Complete catalogue distribution

| Category | IDs | Count | Slot |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Wands | EQP-001 through EQP-015 | 15 | Main Focus or Sidearm |
| Staffs | EQP-016 through EQP-030 | 15 | Main Focus |
| Weapons | EQP-031 through EQP-050 | 20 | Main Focus or Sidearm |
| Armor | EQP-051 through EQP-065 | 15 | Armor |
| Magical clothing | EQP-066 through EQP-080 | 15 | Clothing |
| Boots | EQP-081 through EQP-095 | 15 | Boots |
| Trinkets | EQP-096 through EQP-110 | 15 | Two different legal trinket slots |
| Consumables | EQP-111 through EQP-120 | 10 | Consumable |

The issued plain focus, sidearm, armor, clothing, and boots supply ordinary animations and common actions without bonuses. They are not hidden catalogue purchases. Empty or issued slots remain usable; a player is never unable to cast because their first equipment offers were unhelpful.

## Activation and stacking

The activation field names the logical equipment input and its cost, cooldown, preparation, and charge behavior. All equipment activations map to the one equipped active-item key. The player chooses one enabled active in the shop; other active equipment is dormant with its activation disabled. Consumables have their separate key and one purchased charge. An active item tagged `active_equipment` qualifies prerequisites only when its activation is actually enabled. There are no simultaneous separate armor, boots, wand, and trinket activation keys.

Passive equipment may coexist when its Unique groups differ. A sidearm can use the stated common melee profile and compatible passive effects, but not its special magic activation. Activating a focus or equipment modifier does not grant a separate mastery result, reset the original cooldown, or qualify as a paid exclusive spell for rotation triggers unless its exact record explicitly says so. The universal refund and secondary-event ceilings remain binding.

Round-start reserve shields are issued once and last until broken or the duel ends. Triggered or activated shields have their own short duration and obey the eight-second maximum. All reserve and temporary shielding shares the 100-point cap. Static mana or stamina capacity is equipment capacity rather than passive regeneration; switching between item reserves during combat is prohibited.

Projectiles cannot simultaneously split, ricochet, return, and use portals by merely collecting equipment. Select one compatible trajectory mode during shopping. A wizard’s explicitly chosen trajectory transformation has priority when it conflicts, and the inactive component is visible in the build inspector. Simple speed, cost, and bounded world-strength modifiers can still combine where the record permits them.

## Equipment and augment prerequisites

Owned-item conditions include reserve inventory; equipped-item conditions require the stated occupied slot. A tag-count condition counts distinct equipped definitions with a live relevant effect. Buying two copies of the same definition does not create two legal sources. Different Unique groups matter when the predicate requires distinct groups. A disabled active does not supply an active-effect tag, although an independent enabled passive can still supply its passive tag.

The equipment shop runs before the augment draft. Buy, sell, replace, and set active equipment first, then freeze the loadout for the free draft. A later round can sell a prerequisite item, but dependent augments immediately become dormant when that revised loadout is finalized. Selling never refunds an augment, adds a free choice, or generates new shop cards.

Most item roles connect to universally available actions: moving, landing, common guard, melee, spending mana, changing selected spells, taking a hit, or interacting with terrain. Affinity tools connect to the wizard’s exclusive kit or a natural map source. Pocket Rain can supply water to a Heat wizard; a grounding coat can protect any wizard near a conductive lane. Shared does not mean every conditional effect is equally useful in every matchup.


# Free augments and eligibility specification

The complete 864-augment catalogue consists of 288 shared definitions and 576 wizard-specific spell transformations. Every augmentation and rank is free. Money purchases shared equipment only. At each scheduled draft, five distinct candidates appear, each with its own one-use reroll. One selection ends that draft; unused choices and rerolls are not banked.

The shared catalogue contains 121 compound acquisition predicates. Its unconditional pool contains 43 Silver, 29 Gold, and 16 Prismatic definitions, providing alternatives even when a sophisticated prerequisite chain is unavailable. Each wizard has five Silver, six Gold, and five Prismatic spell transformations. These floors support current-rarity choices and rerolls without granting every wizard access to every transformation.

## Rank and requirement scope

Rank 2 uses one later free draft choice, retains the same slot, and replaces rank 1 according to its exact text. A new definition uses the current draft rarity. A rank 2 of an owned definition may appear at its rarity or a later rarity stage. A Silver parent and its rank 2 can consume the two Silver drafts; a later Gold or Prismatic child must leave enough choices for its other parents. Acquisition plans are checked against the actual draft schedule, not only against numerical rarity ordering.

Wizard identity, round, and completed-duel feats are acquisition-only. Gear, active parent augments, equipped spell profiles, categories, and tag counts are ongoing. A disabled or removed parent cannot qualify descendants. A predicate never evaluates arbitrary script, private future opponent information, local practice events, or an unverified client statement. NOT branches can express a tradeoff, but exclusivity groups enforce mutually exclusive augmentation forms directly.

## Predicate grammar

| Node or leaf | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| all | Every child predicate is true |
| any | At least one child is true |
| not | Its one child is false |
| always | No additional acquisition prerequisite |
| wizard | Exact wizard ID |
| equipped_item | Exact item currently equipped |
| owned_item | Exact item held, including reserve |
| equipped_tag | At least count distinct equipped items supply the tag |
| augment | The exact parent is active at the stated minimum rank |
| spell | Exact spell belongs to the wizard’s owned exclusive kit |
| spell_tag | At least count equipped structural spell profiles have this tag; optional also tags must be on the same qualifying spell |
| spell_tag_exact | Exactly count equipped profiles have this tag |
| spell_distinct_tags | Count distinct tags from the supplied set across qualifying equipped profiles; optional also filters the qualifying profiles |
| spell_cooldown_count | At least count equipped spells meet the declared base cooldown threshold |
| spell_cast_time_count | At least count equipped spells meet the declared intrinsic windup threshold |
| main_focus_category | The Main Focus has the exact category |
| sidearm_category | The Sidearm has the exact category |
| issued_slot | The slot holds only its plain issued equipment |
| slot_tier | The occupied slot has equipment at least the stated tier |
| equipped_category | At least count items occupy legal slots of this category; distinct_unique_groups requires different nonempty groups |
| consumable_charges_at_most | Held purchased charges do not exceed the declared value |
| augment_tag_count | At least count active enumerated parent definitions supply the declared augment tag |
| augment_rank_count | At least count active enumerated parents meet rank_at_least; distinct_families optionally requires different families |
| augment_family_count | Enumerated active parents represent at least count different families |
| round_at_least | Scheduled round number meets the threshold |
| feat | At least the stated number of previous completed duels met the named feat |

Numeric `at_most` and `at_least` thresholds are inclusive. Where a count leaf includes an explicit ID list, only those IDs count. A family-count condition counts distinct families rather than every augmentation in one family. Category counts respect actual equipped slots, so a second trinket is legal while a second armor piece is not. Empty Unique groups cannot satisfy a requirement for different nonempty groups.

School predicates use namespaced tags such as `school:arcane`; damage predicates use `channel:arcane`. This avoids treating every Arcane defense as an Arcane damaging hit. Delivery tags change with wizard transformations and equipment structural changes. General shared effects do not contribute tags to their own eligibility profile; dependencies on other shared effects use explicit augment leaves.

## Dormancy and dependency resolution

Evaluate a finalized loadout in dependency order. First resolve equipment and exclusive spell selection, then wizard transformation legality, structural spell tags, and shared predicates. A dormant augmentation remains owned at its rank and occupies its slot, but supplies no effect, statistics, trigger, tag, or parent qualification. Restoring its ongoing requirements reactivates it at the next finalized preparation or duel start. The UI always displays the missing requirement.

A graph cycle is invalid content. A child cannot qualify itself through a generated tag, require its own future upgrade, or demand more compulsory rarity-stage selections than the match offers. Any alternative branch in a condition must have at least one concrete legal acquisition witness. Rare experimental combinations are checked against slots, active-item limits, effective delivery, prerequisite ranks, and money/tier timing.

After a free choice, the player can replace one owned augmentation, with a confirmation showing any dependent augments that will become dormant. Replacement gives no Crowns and does not reopen the five-card draft. Every next draft reroll works against the new build’s eligibility, with all previously shown definitions excluded for that draft.

## Behavioral transformations

Two dedicated choices per exclusive spell provide alternate trajectories, delayed payloads, traps, recasts, moved fields, directional defenses, summon controls, and reaction timing. Some branches are alternatives; some are compatible dimensions. A transformation states its exact target, rank changes, tradeoff, counterplay, and compatibility group. Source payload, event identity, resource cost, field/summon limits, and other global caps continue to apply.

The draft card shows a before/after description of the final spell form and an exact missing-prerequisite list. A complicated acquisition condition may create a strong and unusual possibility, but its combat effect must still be readable. Neither rarity nor a long prerequisite chain permits an unavoidable hit, unlimited control, or a recursive resource loop.


# Arena materials and generation catalogue

The 24 biomes, 72 modules, and 48 interactive props form a complete procedural kit. Biomes supply art and one declared environmental rule. Modules supply gameplay geometry and sockets. Props supply bounded material interactions. The generator never treats an art name as a collision or damage rule.

## Arena assembly recipe

Each size selects one center module, two spawn alcoves, two mirrored approach chains, one firing lane, two crossover connections, two to four elevation modules, and three to six cover modules. A 24 meter arena uses fewer modules rather than shrinking player scale or narrowing all routes. Larger arenas add routes and useful cover, with approach travel and sightlines still constrained. Material modules replace ordinary floor sections without blocking mandatory movement.

Select three to eight prop definitions per arena, ordinarily two instances of each for parity. Maximum gameplay prop instances are 48. A prop uses its own durability and effect before a module’s generic material defaults. Anchored props may lose functional or cover portions but cannot move. A medium or heavy cover respects the ordinary mass and velocity rules when a force spell strikes it.

Every assembled arena records its chosen modules, transforms, prop definitions, initial material cells, light shafts, gust schedules, and contraction contour. A seed is sufficient to reproduce those choices only with the same ruleset manifest. The server also records the assembled result for replay and support.

## Natural sources and player created fields

Natural arena sources are explicitly previewed map-owned water beds, dust beds, growth beds, conductor sections, or light patches. They do not count against either player’s three-field allocation. Their finite units and any refill schedule are part of the biome rule. There are at most eight active source patches at combat start. Players cannot hide extra gameplay sources inside cosmetic art.

A reaction cloud or temporary field caused by a player counts against that player’s field limit, including a cloud made by striking a prop. The last direct source that commits the reaction owns the bookkeeping allocation. This owner receives no safety exemption: steam, wet conductivity, fire, ice, loose props, and neutral force effects affect both fighters. Simultaneous reactions resolve in the shared server event order, giving one recorded origin for audit.

Environmental damage does not trigger direct spell-hit healing, damage refunds, or equipment chains. A spell’s explicitly declared primary reaction may inherit its source event for attribution, but secondary effects cannot recursively create proc benefits. Destroying natural cover does not count as damaging the opponent. A public terrain reaction can satisfy a completed-duel feat only when its declared feat definition permits it.

## Boundary and final floor validation

At generation, validate at least one route from every currently accessible floor cell to the central final floor under the planned boundary contour. Revalidate that route after permitted destruction and player-created walls. A placement that would seal the last remaining approach fails visibly and refunds its placement cost; it does not become invisible collision.

At 83 seconds, mark final-center soft cover and optional high ledges that will leave the legal duel space. At 85 seconds, map-owned soft cover in the final center retires, leaving the anchored eight-meter floor. Player-created temporary fields can retain their stated lifetime, but cannot remove that floor, place a permanent roof over it, or violate route/field caps. Both players receive the same warning.

## Counterplay and visual standards

Water edges show cell connectivity; insulation has a distinct border pattern. Conductors glow before discharge. Ice shows fracture stages and impact direction. Combustible growth visibly exhausts its fuel. Prisms show a fixed face and reflected ray segment. Acoustic props produce public sounds from their actual location. Movable covers display tracks or mass cues. An active cloud’s edge has consistent visibility at every graphics quality.

A biome’s cosmetic darkness, rain, snow, and dust never secretly changes enemy visibility, movement, or resource regeneration. Its one gameplay modifier is listed explicitly. If a future map needs a second modifier, it requires a new biome definition and preview rather than an undocumented art exception. Ranked generation uses functional parity; a custom host may opt into asymmetry with a visible rule fingerprint.

The following catalogues specify all biomes, modules, and props. Footprints include their connecting clear space. Height is relative to connected floor, not a hidden fall-damage multiplier. Generic module durability yields to the exact attached prop or cover definition, and anchored load-bearing geometry remains stable.


# Worked builds and conditional progression

The 48 worked examples turn the catalogue into concrete loadout plans. The first 36 give one plan for each wizard, with six equipped exclusive spells, three spell transformations, three shared augments, and a compatible shared equipment set. Each plan uses two Silver, two Gold, and two Prismatic free selections at rounds 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, and 11. Transformations target different spells to show multi-spell interactions without concealing a branch conflict.

The remaining twelve examples demonstrate acquisition conditions: a shared weapon and armor requirement, two differently grouped trinkets, a parent augmentation, a completed-duel feat, no active equipment, a school-aligned kit, a plain issued armor slot, and two rank 2 augments from different families. An example is a possible draft path. It does not guarantee the required random cards will appear or declare the build optimal.

## Reading a build

The equipment cost is the total final gear purchase price, excluding issued items. Purchase each tier only after its scheduled unlock and preserve money when a useful offer is absent. The list is a target loadout rather than a requirement to buy every item in the first shop. Equipment drawn or bought differently can support the same broad plan.

A transformation interaction quotes its exact rank 1 change. Read it together with the target base spell, then apply equipment, shared augments, one mastery reward, and global caps. Do not add the source payload again when a transformation transfers part of it into a delayed hit or field. Recasts and secondary effects inherit their declared budgets and cannot generate another mastery result.

Each build's action sequence explains when to use its grammar and common movement, weapon, or defensive tools. Counterplay belongs to the complete opponent plan: break preparation, change route, avoid an exposed windup, contest an anchor, force a missed cadence, or punish recovery. A legal build has strengths and openings rather than an automatic win condition.

## Conditional example with ranks

Two Defended Theses illustrates a long route. In Silver, choose Guard Economy rank 1, then its rank 2. In Gold, choose Full Breath rank 1, then rank 2. Those are two augmentation families, occupying two slots but consuming four free choices. Equip Pocket Reservoir and Marathon Bead, two passive trinkets with different Unique groups. A Prismatic Double Thesis can now appear. Taking it is the fifth free choice; the sixth can select one wizard transformation. Removing either parent or a required trinket makes the dependent effect dormant.

This route deliberately trades four different early augments for two deeper ranks and a late conditional payoff. The same total number of free choices is available to every player. Crowns pay for the trinkets, not for the ranks or the late augment. The player can abandon the plan if drafts or equipment offers favor another direction.

## Adapting to the arena and opponent

Before an equipment shop, inspect the generated biome and opponent's previous completed loadout. Water, combustible growth, prisms, conductive rails, and moved cover can make a carried item useful even when the wizard cannot create that material itself. A Heat kit can spend a Pocket Rain consumable or use a natural pool to form steam; a different wizard can clear or exploit the resulting neutral cloud.

Keep six exclusive spells suited to the immediate opponent, remembering that changing their structural tags can make a conditional augment dormant. A transformed projectile trap no longer qualifies as a projectile merely because its base form did. Gear and augment decisions can preserve a build identity while changing one defensive action, approach route, or payoff spell. The searchable catalogue allows those changes to be reviewed through stable IDs.




# Wizard roster

36 complete definitions.

## WIZ-001 Ilyra Voss

**Title:** The Lenskeeper

**Casting mode:** Held reticle convergence: sustained focus narrows two aim rings.

**Input sequence:** Hold primary for 0.20–0.70 s while aiming; release to cast. Cast Modifier displays a target-sized practice guide; it never chooses a target.

**Normal cast:** Release after at least 0.20 s for the spell’s normal effect. Releasing earlier queues a normal cast at 0.20 s; cancel releases the queue without spending.

**Mastery:** Keep the aim vector within a 2-degree cone for the final 0.25 s and release with rings aligned: next direct spell gains 12% projectile speed, or 12% lower windup for nonprojectile spells, never both. Moving targets still require manual tracking.

**Signature:** Lens Split — 16 s cooldown, 20 mana, 0.30 s windup. Place two visible glass screens, each 1.5 m wide with 30 health, within 6 m for 3 s. Any projectile crossing one screen loses 15% speed once, including the caster’s; melee destroys screens normally. They do not block sight, hitscan, or movement and occupy one field allocation together.

**Passive:** Clear Focus — after standing or walking without sprint for 0.8 s, the next ranged direct spell costs 5% less mana; resets on cast, sprint, or dodge. Combines within the 20% casting-efficiency limit.

**Range preference:** Long range; seeks stable lanes.

**Weakness:** Focus gives opponents a readable line and loses its reward when forced to flick suddenly.

**Counterplay:** Break sight with steam or cover, attack from changing elevations, and close during the held focus. Walk around or strike Lens Split screens.

**Exclusive kit:** SPL-001, SPL-002, SPL-003, SPL-004, SPL-005, SPL-006, SPL-007, SPL-008

**Default six spells:** SPL-001, SPL-002, SPL-003, SPL-004, SPL-005, SPL-006

**Lore:** A former observatory surveyor treats battle as measurement under pressure.

**Visual identity:** Brass sight rings, a cropped cobalt mantle, and visibly converging concentric light.

**Audio identity:** Quiet glass chimes rising toward a single clean release tone.

**Difficulty:** 2

**Tags:** aim, held-focus, Light, ranged

## WIZ-002 Bram Cinder

**Title:** The Kilnheart

**Casting mode:** Pressure release: charge a forge gauge and vent at its crest.

**Input sequence:** Hold primary for 0.20–0.60 s; a single visible gauge rises and falls. Release selects the cast time, with an audible crest cue.

**Normal cast:** Any release after 0.20 s casts normally. Overholding at 0.60 s auto-vents a normal cast; there is no random misfire or self-damage.

**Mastery:** Release within the marked 100 ms crest window at 0.45 s: direct damage gains 12%. On nondamaging spells, pay 12% less mana instead. One reward per spell.

**Signature:** Kiln Vent — 14 s cooldown, 25 mana, 0.35 s windup. Project a visible 4 m cone that deals 28 thermal damage and pushes enemies 1.5 m. It contributes Heat strength 1 to affected world props; it does not create a persistent fire field.

**Passive:** Tempered Hands — taking thermal damage grants a visible 20-point shield for 2 s, once per 8 s. It provides no thermal immunity and respects the shared shield cap.

**Range preference:** Mid and close range; release timing rewards deliberate peeks.

**Weakness:** Crest timing is predictable, and the cone requires commitment at short range.

**Counterplay:** Peek between pressure cues, force an early release, then punish the cone’s windup. Move sideways out of the cone.

**Exclusive kit:** SPL-009, SPL-010, SPL-011, SPL-012, SPL-013, SPL-014, SPL-015, SPL-016

**Default six spells:** SPL-009, SPL-010, SPL-011, SPL-012, SPL-013, SPL-014

**Lore:** An industrial spellwright who once kept floating foundries aloft.

**Visual identity:** Soot-black apron armor, a glowing chest furnace emblem, red pressure bands on the focus.

**Audio identity:** A building bellows hiss and a metallic crest ping heard by nearby opponents.

**Difficulty:** 2

**Tags:** release-timing, Heat, midrange

## WIZ-003 Sera Quill

**Title:** The Living Script

**Casting mode:** Rune tracing: draw a selected spell’s stable three-stroke glyph.

**Input sequence:** Tap primary for a guided 0.30 s normal inscription. Hold Cast Modifier to open an explicitly camera-locked rune pane, trace its three strokes, then release primary. Cancel instantly returns view control. Direction-key tracing is equivalent.

**Normal cast:** The guided inscription always yields normal output. A manual trace with the right three-stroke order but low shape accuracy also yields normal output; invalid or abandoned strokes do not spend resources.

**Mastery:** Finish the three strokes within 0.75 s with at least 85% path accuracy and endpoints within 8% of pane width: the spell costs 15% less mana. Shape scoring uses normalized pane coordinates, never raw mouse DPI.

**Signature:** Revision Seal — 18 s cooldown, 20 mana, 0.30 s windup. Place a glowing 1.5 m radius floor seal within 8 m for 4 s, 40 health. Any spell projectile crossing it loses 10% speed once, including the caster’s. The seal occupies one field allocation.

**Passive:** Margin Notes — canceling a prepared spell before commitment restores normal camera control and gives 10 stamina, at most once per 8 s. It never refunds spent spell mana or adds damage.

**Range preference:** Mid range; favors cover for inscription.

**Weakness:** Manual glyphs temporarily demand attention away from the battlefield and advertise ink movement.

**Counterplay:** Pressure the pane window, destroy Revision Seal, and shift position before the completed spell is aimed.

**Exclusive kit:** SPL-017, SPL-018, SPL-019, SPL-020, SPL-021, SPL-022, SPL-023, SPL-024

**Default six spells:** SPL-017, SPL-018, SPL-019, SPL-020, SPL-021, SPL-022

**Lore:** A court archivist whose forbidden marginalia became physically real.

**Visual identity:** Ivory cuffs, floating black script, and gold writing nibs; all glyphs use fixed readable silhouettes.

**Audio identity:** Three dry pen strokes and a resonant stamp at commitment.

**Difficulty:** 4

**Tags:** gesture, Sand, preparation

## WIZ-004 Oren Vey

**Title:** The True Utterance

**Casting mode:** Spoken syllable cadence with an equivalent rhythm-key language.

**Input sequence:** Hold primary to select the spell’s displayed three-syllable phrase, speak it during the 0.75 s cadence, then release to commit. Alternatively use three rhythm inputs at the same cadence. A normal cast uses the guided cadence with broad 200 ms beat tolerance.

**Normal cast:** Recognized selected syllables in order, or the three equivalent keys, cast normally. A recognition failure displays the missing syllable and permits the rhythm alternative; no resource is spent until commitment.

**Mastery:** Score all three syllables or key taps within 80 ms of their beats: pay 15% less mana. Pronunciation scores only distinguish selected syllables; accent, voice pitch, loudness, and vocal strain never improve damage.

**Signature:** Hush Verse — 20 s cooldown, 25 mana, 0.40 s windup. Fire a visible 18 m/s Sound ring up to 12 m, radius 0.8 m. First enemy hit takes 18 arcane damage and is silenced for 0.4 s, sharing global hard-control immunity. Cover stops the ring.

**Passive:** Measured Voice — a completed normal or mastered phrase grants 6 stamina once per 4 s. A player can obtain the identical passive using rhythm input.

**Range preference:** Mid range; values uninterrupted phrases.

**Weakness:** Every phrase has the same committed duration and an audible opponent-facing chant generated by the game even in key mode.

**Counterplay:** Use cover during the chant, pressure while syllables are being entered, and dodge Hush Verse’s slow visible ring.

**Exclusive kit:** SPL-025, SPL-026, SPL-027, SPL-028, SPL-029, SPL-030, SPL-031, SPL-032

**Default six spells:** SPL-025, SPL-026, SPL-027, SPL-028, SPL-029, SPL-030

**Lore:** A linguist reconstructing the words that once held a broken moon together.

**Visual identity:** A silver throat clasp, amber phoneme rings, and embroidery resembling sound waves.

**Audio identity:** Three unambiguous game-generated syllables; microphone volume never changes the opponent’s cue.

**Difficulty:** 3

**Tags:** voice, rhythm-alternative, Sound, midrange

## WIZ-005 Vexa Noll

**Title:** The Formula Runner

**Casting mode:** Ordered key assembly: a prefix, operator, and closure.

**Input sequence:** Hold Cast Modifier and enter the selected spell’s fixed three-token sequence using Modifier A, Modifier B, and primary; aim and movement remain live. Tokens are displayed during training and optionally in combat.

**Normal cast:** Complete the correct order within 1.2 s, with no beat requirement, then primary commits. A wrong token clears only that token and adds a visible 0.15 s correction delay; no mana is spent.

**Mastery:** Complete all three tokens within 0.45 s without correction: gain 10% shorter intrinsic spell windup, capped at a 0.06 s reduction. Does not reduce spell cooldown or remove enemy telegraphs.

**Signature:** Factor Shift — 15 s cooldown, 15 mana, instant. For 3 s, the next spell may be canceled during the first 50% of its intrinsic windup; cancellation consumes 5 mana and starts 25% of its normal cooldown. Normal spell costs are spent only if committed.

**Passive:** Clean Syntax — after two different normal spell definitions are committed consecutively, the next different spell costs 5% less mana; same-spell repetition breaks the sequence. One bonus per third cast, within efficiency caps.

**Range preference:** Mid range; fluid offense through changing formulas.

**Weakness:** Token correction costs time; repeatedly using one safe spell yields no passive benefit.

**Counterplay:** Interrupt her intended cadence with cover and aggression, then punish an incorrect or canceled preparation.

**Exclusive kit:** SPL-033, SPL-034, SPL-035, SPL-036, SPL-037, SPL-038, SPL-039, SPL-040

**Default six spells:** SPL-033, SPL-034, SPL-035, SPL-036, SPL-037, SPL-038

**Lore:** A magical compiler engineer who considers dueling a proof of execution.

**Visual identity:** Geometric violet coat panels and three rotating punctuation glyphs around the hands.

**Audio identity:** A distinct click for each token and a low error tick for corrections.

**Difficulty:** 3

**Tags:** ordered-keys, Arcane, APM

## WIZ-006 Cael Argent

**Title:** The Returnblade

**Casting mode:** Parry-triggered casting: turn a timed defense into an empowered spell preparation.

**Input sequence:** Primary performs a 0.25 s normal preparation. During a successful common parry, press Cast Modifier within 0.5 s to arm the next selected spell; release primary to cast while manual aim remains required.

**Normal cast:** Normal preparation is always available. A failed parry uses the common parry stamina cost and recovery and never disables casting.

**Mastery:** A parry performed within its final 100 ms success band arms one spell for 2 s: that spell has 12% shorter intrinsic windup. The reward applies once, cannot stack, and does not reflect the spell automatically.

**Signature:** Argent Lunge — 14 s cooldown, 25 stamina, 0.20 s tell. Dash up to 5 m in the aimed ground direction and make a 2.5 m melee thrust for 35 physical damage. Terrain stops the dash; it has no invulnerability and uses the shared two-dash-charge cap.

**Passive:** Return Guard — a successful common parry grants 15 shield for 1.5 s, once per 6 s. Shield is awarded after damage prevention resolves and cannot absorb the triggering hit retroactively.

**Range preference:** Close range with a midrange countercast.

**Weakness:** Needs opponents to offer readable attacks, and mistakes consume stamina needed for approach.

**Counterplay:** Feint windups, use indirect fields, vary attack timing, and step sideways from the lunge tell.

**Exclusive kit:** SPL-041, SPL-042, SPL-043, SPL-044, SPL-045, SPL-046, SPL-047, SPL-048

**Default six spells:** SPL-041, SPL-042, SPL-043, SPL-044, SPL-045, SPL-046

**Lore:** A disgraced royal bodyguard hunting the spell that killed his charge.

**Visual identity:** Polished silver vambraces, a narrow dueling mask, and bright parry sparks.

**Audio identity:** A sharp steel note on a parry and a drawn-out scrape before the lunge.

**Difficulty:** 4

**Tags:** parry, Metal, melee

## WIZ-007 Mira Bell

**Title:** The Tempo Witch

**Casting mode:** Instrument rhythm: build a beat and release on a chosen measure.

**Input sequence:** Holding primary starts a visible four-beat staff using eighth-note beats at 120 BPM, 0.25 s apart. Tap Modifier A on two adjacent beats and primary on the following beat to cast. The staff stops after casting; no real instrument is required.

**Normal cast:** Three inputs within broad 120 ms beat windows cast normally. The player can use a guided 0.50 s phrase with the same total commitment and normal output. Guidance does not award mastery.

**Mastery:** Three inputs each within 70 ms of their beats grant 12% lower mana cost. Repeating on additional measures earns no greater bonus and cannot bank multiple casts.

**Signature:** Offbeat Pulse — 16 s cooldown, 20 mana, 0.30 s windup. Emit a visible 5 m radius ring for 24 arcane damage; struck enemies suffer a 15% slow for 1.2 s. The ring propagates at 10 m/s, requires sight at impact, and can be outrun or blocked by cover.

**Passive:** Walking Meter — after two different spell casts at least 0.5 s apart, grant 8 stamina, once per 6 s. Running faster or tapping extra beats grants nothing.

**Range preference:** Mid range and mobile close-range disruption.

**Weakness:** Predictable beats expose launch timing; the ring is weak outside its short reach.

**Counterplay:** Peek between beats, cross cover during the ring, and make her restart a interrupted phrase.

**Exclusive kit:** SPL-049, SPL-050, SPL-051, SPL-052, SPL-053, SPL-054, SPL-055, SPL-056

**Default six spells:** SPL-049, SPL-050, SPL-051, SPL-052, SPL-053, SPL-054

**Lore:** An itinerant musician who learned the resonant intervals of stone and flesh.

**Visual identity:** Bronze handbells, teal pleated robes, and metronome ticks orbiting the focus.

**Audio identity:** A fixed opponent-facing beat count; personal music sliders cannot hide cast cues.

**Difficulty:** 3

**Tags:** instrument, rhythm, Sound, movement

## WIZ-008 Dain Coil

**Title:** The Circuit Saint

**Casting mode:** Charge routing: connect a source, junction, and destination in a three-node circuit.

**Input sequence:** Hold Cast Modifier; select one of three displayed junctions with Modifier A/B or primary, then confirm the glowing destination. Aim stays live; the circuit occupies a small fixed HUD corner.

**Normal cast:** Any valid source-to-destination route completed within 1 s casts normally. Unconnected routes remain in preparation and spend nothing.

**Mastery:** Use the shortest two-edge route shown for the selected spell within 0.55 s: gain 15% resource efficiency. The graph changes only when a different spell is selected, never randomly during preparation.

**Signature:** Ground Lead — 18 s cooldown, 20 mana, 0.35 s windup. Place a destructible 35-health rod within 8 m for 5 s. It absorbs up to 40 electrical damage delivered into its 1.5 m radius from either player, then breaks. It never absorbs damage already assigned to a player outside that radius and occupies one field allocation.

**Passive:** Insulated Step — crossing an explicitly connected electrified wet patch costs 20% less stamina for the next dodge within 2 s, once per 8 s; electrical damage is still taken normally.

**Range preference:** Mid range; rewards readable reaction terrain.

**Weakness:** Routing attention competes with aiming, and his rod has no protection against other channels.

**Counterplay:** Attack from mixed channels, destroy the rod with physical hits, and force a route correction through sudden pressure.

## WIZ-009 Nessa Vale

**Title:** The Surveyor

**Casting mode:** Sigil geometry: place three vertices and close a stable shape.

**Input sequence:** Hold Cast Modifier to display a three-vertex local sigil pane. Place its vertices with three taps while the pane explicitly holds the camera; release to resume aim and primary commits. Equivalent three direction-key selections use the same pane and commitment.

**Normal cast:** Any non-self-crossing triangle completed within 1.2 s casts normally. The resulting world spell still launches from the caster’s usual origin and uses the normal range.

**Mastery:** Match the shown area within 10% and the longest edge within 10%, in at most 0.75 s: a nondamaging spell costs 15% less mana; a damaging spell gains 10% projectile speed. At most one reward.

**Signature:** Survey Wall — 18 s cooldown, 30 mana, 0.50 s windup. Raise a 2 m wide, 1.3 m tall, 50-health Earth parapet within 6 m for 4 s. It blocks projectiles and movement, cannot spawn intersecting a player, and occupies one field allocation.

**Passive:** Measured Ground — while within 2 m of a destructible construct she created, receive 5% physical damage reduction. Multiple constructs do not stack; total damage-reduction cap still applies.

**Range preference:** Mid range and deliberate terrain fighting.

**Weakness:** Geometric casting has a clearly signaled attention window; small parapets offer limited cover.

**Counterplay:** Flank or jump the parapet, destroy it, and pressure during vertex placement.

## WIZ-010 Halen Tide

**Title:** The Breathless Diver

**Casting mode:** Pressure metering: maintain a virtual breath gauge with alternating compression and vent.

**Input sequence:** Hold primary to compress the gauge; Modifier A vents it. Release primary between 0.30 and 0.90 s to cast. This is a game meter, with no microphone, lung capacity, or breath holding requirement.

**Normal cast:** Any release in the safe 20–80 pressure band casts normally. Leaving the band automatically vents and offers a normal cast after 0.30 s; mana is spent only on that cast.

**Mastery:** Keep pressure within 45–55 for a continuous 0.25 s before release: pay 15% less mana. Faster toggling than the 0.1 s accepted input interval adds no benefit.

**Signature:** Undertow Mantle — 17 s cooldown, 20 mana, 0.25 s windup. Create a neutral 2 m radius Water eddy centered at the cast location for 3 s. Enemies and caster within it are slowed 15%; each body takes only 12 arcane damage on first entry. Water strength 1; one field allocation.

**Passive:** Pressure Reserve — after spending at least 30 mana on one committed spell, gain 10 stamina, once per 6 s. Refunds and subsequent reaction costs cannot retrigger it.

**Range preference:** Mid and close range; likes paths through water.

**Weakness:** Pressure maintenance consumes attention, and the eddy hinders him as well.

**Counterplay:** Change angles while his meter is stable, attack from outside the eddy, and use Heat or Frost to alter its water.

**Tags:** pressure-meter, Water, reactions

## WIZ-011 Tess Meridian

**Title:** The Pendulum Judge

**Casting mode:** Phase selection: a moving pendulum crosses attack, utility, and guard sectors.

**Input sequence:** Primary starts a 0.60 s pendulum sweep; primary again commits in the sector matching the selected spell’s displayed function. Modifier A stops the sweep for a normal 0.30 s cast if timing is undesirable.

**Normal cast:** Any second press casts normally; stopping the sweep also casts normally. Function tags are fixed in each spell record, and no hidden random sector exists.

**Weakness:** Sector timing narrows launch opportunities; the miss refund is too small to support deliberate spam.

## WIZ-013 Liora Thread

**Title:** The Anchorwitch

**Casting mode:** Tether geometry: prepare a spell while maintaining distance to a declared anchor.

**Input sequence:** Tap Cast Modifier to place a harmless visible anchor on nearby ground within 6 m; primary begins a 0.30 s tether preparation. Move while aiming to adjust the displayed anchor distance, then release primary. One anchor only; 6 s lifetime.

**Normal cast:** Any release casts normally, even outside the anchor band. With no anchor, primary uses an ordinary 0.30 s preparation.

**Mastery:** Remain 2–4 m from the anchor and keep the tether unbroken by cover for the final 0.30 s: gain 12% lower mana cost. Range is checked server-side and does not extend spell reach.

**Signature:** Snapline — 16 s cooldown, 20 mana, 0.30 s windup. Attach a visible line to the first enemy hit by a 20 m/s projectile within 10 m for 1.5 s. If the line stays unobstructed, the target is slowed 15%; line breaks past 10 m or on solid cover. No pull and no reveal through walls.

**Passive:** Sure Footing — while inside the 2–4 m anchor band, common dodge costs 5 less stamina, once per 5 s. The anchor is nonphysical and supplies no shield or sight information.

**Range preference:** Mid range; orbits an announced fighting position.

**Weakness:** An anchor advertises preferred positioning, and cover can break the mastery tether.

**Counterplay:** Move beyond her anchor band, contest its perimeter, and break Snapline using terrain.

## WIZ-014 Fen Skystep

**Title:** The Footwork Adept

**Casting mode:** Directional footwork: two meaningful movement changes form a cast pattern.

**Input sequence:** Hold primary during two chosen movement-direction changes, then release. A direction counts only after moving at least 0.5 m, so vibrating movement keys does nothing. Sprint and camera aim remain normal.

**Normal cast:** Release after one qualifying step or after a 0.35 s guided preparation for normal output. Jumping is never required for a normal cast.

**Mastery:** Complete a forward-to-sideways or sideways-to-backward pattern within 0.9 s while traveling at least 1.5 m: the spell gains 12% projectile speed, or pays 12% less mana if nonprojectile. Terrain collisions invalidate only the reward.

**Signature:** Slipstream Cut — 14 s cooldown, 25 stamina, 0.20 s tell. Dash 4 m sideways and leave a neutral 1.5 m wide wind corridor for 2 s. Projectiles crossing it deflect 5 degrees in its visible arrow direction once. No damage or invulnerability; one field allocation.

**Passive:** Light Landing — landing after a normal jump restores 5 stamina if at least 1 m horizontal travel occurred, once per 5 s. It cannot restore more than the jump’s paid cost.

**Range preference:** Close and mid range; constantly changes angles.

**Weakness:** Mastery requires space and exposes travel direction; narrow terrain constrains footwork.

**Range preference:** Mid range with sustained lateral motion.

**Weakness:** Vector mastery is telegraphed by committed travel and performs poorly in cramped corners.

**Counterplay:** Lead shots along his declared run, force reversals with cover, and punish the fixed reverse dash.

## WIZ-030 Anwen Circle

**Title:** The Ritual Walker

**Casting mode:** World ritual traversal: step through two visible ground marks before casting.

**Input sequence:** Cast Modifier lays two harmless 0.5 m ground marks at reachable positions 1 m apart near the caster for 3 s. Walk through them in displayed order, then primary commits. Marks cannot cross solid cover or create an inaccessible path.

**Normal cast:** Primary alone casts normally after 0.35 s. Walking through one mark and committing also gives normal output. Marks require no mana and have no collision or reaction strength.

**Mastery:** Traverse both marks within 0.9 s and cast within 0.25 s of the second: pay 15% less mana. Teleporting or being knocked across marks does not qualify; path is chosen by the caster’s aim.

**Signature:** Circle of Return — 21 s cooldown, 25 mana, 0.40 s windup. Place a visible 40-health return circle at current ground position for 3 s. Re-activate once to teleport back if within 6 m and destination clear; the circle shatters if blocked or destroyed. No invulnerability; teleport uses global cap. One field allocation.

**Passive:** Pilgrim’s Rest — completing a ritual traversal grants 8 stamina once per 6 s, including normal one-mark traversal. No passive health regeneration.

**Range preference:** Mid range with planned retreats.

**Weakness:** Both ritual path and return destination are public and can be contested.

**Counterplay:** Aim along the marks, destroy the return circle, or stand near its destination to punish return.

## WIZ-031 Korr Etch

**Casting mode:** Kinetic engraving: deliberate weapon-shaped arcs inscribe a spell without requiring a hit.

**Input sequence:** Hold Cast Modifier and use the normal melee-direction selection to choose horizontal or vertical air cuts; perform two 0.20 s non-damaging inscription cuts, then primary commits. Inscription cuts have visible hand motion and do not secretly become melee attacks.

**Normal cast:** Any two cuts cast normally. A guided one-cut normal preparation takes 0.35 s. Weapon category changes appearance only; all focuses can inscribe.

**Mastery:** Choose the selected spell’s fixed perpendicular cut pair and reverse each exactly within its 100 ms endpoint cue: gain 12% direct damage, or 12% mana efficiency for nondamaging spells. Cuts consume no stamina because they cause no attack.

## WIZ-032 Vela Red

**Casting mode:** Vitality commitment: choose a small visible health pledge and confirm it at cast release.

## WIZ-033 Sion Palimpsest

**Title:** The Clause Reader

**Casting mode:** Conditional parsing: choose the correct branch of a displayed spell sentence.

**Input sequence:** Cast Modifier shows a fixed two-clause rule for the selected spell, such as “if grounded choose left, otherwise choose right.” Select the true branch with A/B, then primary commits after 0.30 s. Conditions use the caster’s plainly visible state only.

**Normal cast:** Either branch still casts normally. State is sampled when the sentence opens and stays frozen for the preparation; it cannot change secretly between selection and commitment.

**Mastery:** Choose the true branch within 0.35 s and commit within another 0.20 s: pay 15% less mana. The sentence library is fixed and learnable; choices never involve guessing a concealed opponent or unknown status.

First enemy hit takes 22 arcane damage and has an active soft slow shortened by up to 0.5 s while gaining a new 20% slow for 1 s; stronger-slow-only rules apply, so it cannot stack.

**Passive:** Second Draft — after making a wrong branch selection, the next correct normal cast within 3 s restores 4 mana, once per 8 s and capped at 25% of its paid cost. Errors never produce extra damage.

**Range preference:** Mid range; decisions under changing self-state.

**Weakness:** Branch reading has mental overhead, and choosing incorrectly grants no mastery advantage.

**Counterplay:** Pressure while clauses are visible, vary engagement range, and evade the ribbon’s straight visible path.

## WIZ-035 Halvek Oath

**Title:** The Eventbinder

**Casting mode:** Declared event casting: select a near-term public event and release in response.

**Input sequence:** Cast Modifier declares one of three events: own landing, own common melee recovery ending, or own spell cooldown becoming ready. Primary arms one spell for up to 1.5 s; press primary again to release manually or on the chosen event cue.

**Normal cast:** Manual release after 0.30 s always gives normal output. Arming does not spend mana; timeout cancels. No enemy action must occur and no event auto-aims or auto-fires.

**Mastery:** Release within 100 ms after the declared event’s cue: gain 12% lower mana cost. Events must originate from genuine gameplay actions; repeated harmless button toggles cannot create an event.

**Signature:** Oathpost — 20 s cooldown, 25 mana, 0.40 s windup. Plant a visible 45-health post within 6 m for 4 s. If the caster casts within 2 m of it, the first committed cast grants 25 shield for 1.5 s, then post expires. No bonus if it is destroyed; one field allocation.

**Passive:** Kept Word — completing two different declared events across separate casts grants 10 stamina, once per 7 s. Manual releases do not qualify but remain normal casts.

**Range preference:** Close and mid range; responsive transitions after actions.

**Weakness:** Armed spells can expire before a chosen event, and Oathpost announces a valuable position.

**Counterplay:** Force movement away from the post, delay or deny his follow-up actions, and attack just before the expected event release.

**Exclusive kit:** SPL-273, SPL-274, SPL-275, SPL-276, SPL-277, SPL-278, SPL-279, SPL-280

**Default six spells:** SPL-273, SPL-274, SPL-275, SPL-276, SPL-277, SPL-278

**Tags:** event-response, Earth, transitions

## WIZ-036 Nami Drift

**Title:** The Guided Ember

**Casting mode:** Cursor shepherding: guide a virtual drifting mote through two gates with controlled corrections.

**Input sequence:** Hold Cast Modifier to open a fixed corner widget; A/B apply left/right steering impulses to a mote while it drifts upward for 0.60 s. Primary commits at the top. Aim and movement remain live; the widget never steers world projectiles.

**Normal cast:** Reaching the top at any horizontal position yields normal output. Guided mode follows the center channel and takes the same 0.60 s preparation without the mastery reward.

**Mastery:** Pass both gate centers within 8% of widget width using at most four steering impulses: pay 15% less mana. The same selected spell has the same gate layout; rapid repeated taps reduce control rather than granting power.

**Signature:** Drift Fan — 16 s cooldown, 20 mana, 0.30 s windup. Create a neutral 3 m-wide by 5 m-long wind lane within 6 m for 3 s. Steam inside moves 2 m/s along its visible arrow; bodies inside receive a 10% movement-speed increase in the arrow direction, capped by global speed limits. No damage; one field allocation.

**Passive:** Small Corrections — after walking at least 2 m without sprint or dodge, the next spell refunds 4 mana on a direct hit, once per 6 s, no more than 25% of paid cost. Proc damage cannot trigger it.

**Range preference:** Mid range; controls sightlines and steady movement.

**Weakness:** Shepherding takes the longest fixed preparation, and wind lanes can assist an opponent equally.

**Counterplay:** Push during the 0.60 s widget, travel with her wind when useful, and reposition after steam moves.

**Exclusive kit:** SPL-281, SPL-282, SPL-283, SPL-284, SPL-285, SPL-286, SPL-287, SPL-288

**Default six spells:** SPL-281, SPL-282, SPL-283, SPL-284, SPL-285, SPL-286

**Audio identity:** Soft fan snaps, two gate chimes, and a continuous wind-lane flutter.

**Difficulty:** 3

**Tags:** cursor-control, Heat, world-interactions

# Free augments and spell transformations

864 complete definitions.

## AUG-001 Steady Hand

**Family:** Casting mastery

**Condition:** Release a direct projectile after keeping aim within a 1-degree cone for 0.3 s. Draft requirement: at least one projectile spell equipped.

**Rank one:** Gain 6% projectile speed.

**Rank two:** Gain 10% projectile speed.

**Drawback:** Sprinting resets preparation.

**Tags:** mastery, precision, projectile

**Counterplay:** Force tracking changes before release.

**Wizard scope:** None or unrestricted

**Rarity:** Silver

**Eligibility predicate:** `{"spell_tag": {"tag": "projectile", "count": 1}}`

**Transformation compatibility group:** None

**Target spells:** None or unrestricted

## AUG-002 Measured Breath

**Family:** Casting mastery

**Condition:** Complete an optional advanced voice or equivalent rhythm variation. Draft requirement: Oren Vey, using spoken syllables or equivalent rhythm keys.

**Rank one:** Paid cast costs 6% less mana.

**Rank two:** Paid cast costs 10% less mana.

**Drawback:** Benefit requires full normal cast commitment and audible telegraph.

**Tags:** mastery, voice, rhythm, mana

**Counterplay:** Pressure during the spoken or rhythmic commitment.

**Wizard scope:** None or unrestricted

**Rarity:** Silver

**Eligibility predicate:** `{"any": [{"wizard": "WIZ-004"}]}`

**Transformation compatibility group:** None

**Target spells:** None or unrestricted

## AUG-003 Clean Glyph

**Family:** Casting mastery

**Condition:** Complete optional gesture variation with no more than one correction. Draft requirement: a tracing/geometry/engraving wizard: WIZ-003,009,025 or 031.

**Rank one:** Paid cast costs 6% less mana.

**Rank two:** Paid cast costs 10% less mana.

**Drawback:** Aim remains committed to the gesture until completion.

**Tags:** mastery, gesture, mana

**Counterplay:** Rush during gesture input.

**Wizard scope:** None or unrestricted

**Rarity:** Silver

**Eligibility predicate:** `{"any": [{"wizard": "WIZ-003"}, {"wizard": "WIZ-009"}, {"wizard": "WIZ-025"}, {"wizard": "WIZ-031"}]}`

**Transformation compatibility group:** None

**Target spells:** None or unrestricted

## AUG-004 Ordered Mind

**Family:** Casting mastery
